Lunch with Lalremsiami from HR today. I asked her, casually, where the leave policies were. She raised an eyebrow and smiled but didn't ask questions. Bless her.
Tonight Bikash and I read both our companies' policies line by line at the dining table. Mine: maternity leave paid in full for the standard period, then the option of unpaid extra months. His: paternity leave of two weeks. He was annoyed. "Two weeks? That's nothing." He's going to ask if he can add some of his annual leave.
Then the harder bit: if I take four extra unpaid months, how much less do we have coming in? We wrote it down month by month. It's a real gap.
So the plan: save a fixed amount every month for the next year into a separate account, until the gap is covered. Only then, we try.
I feel oddly calm. Like the unknown just got a shape.
— Urmila

Today was the check-up. Finally.
For two months I'd been reading forums at midnight. One said eat this, another said never eat that. Keerthana's mother-in-law told her a list of rules that contradicted all of them. Rohit's aunt had her own theories about which month is "lucky". My head was spinning.
So Rohit said, "Let's just ask a real doctor." We booked an appointment with Dr. Kulkarni, a gynaecologist at the clinic near the station.
She was calm and kind. She asked about our health and history, suggested some routine tests, and talked through general habits. When I brought up the forum stuff, she smiled and said, "Bring your questions to me instead. Every person is different."
We came out with a printed sheet and a follow-up date. Rohit deleted two forum apps on the auto ride home.
I feel so much lighter.
— Aditi

Dear Chandrika,

Thank you for the little socks. Zoe wears them every day.
You asked how we're doing. Honestly, the first month nearly broke me. Our plan was that I'd do every night feed, since I'm on leave and Arif goes back to the bank. It made sense on paper.
By week four I was falling asleep standing at the stove. I snapped at Arif for breathing too loudly. He found me crying in the bathroom one night and said, "This plan isn't working. We change it."
Now we alternate nights. On my off-nights I sleep in the other room with earplugs. We also found an aunty from our building who comes three mornings a week so I can nap.
And every Sunday we ask each other: "How are you actually doing?" Not the baby. Us.
I feel human again, mostly.

Love,
Sabina
